findings.observation: Sheet 5 contains a section titled 'AUSTIN ENERGY STANDARD NOTES' with 5 numbered notes. The first 4 notes address all required topics: (1) tree pruning/easement rights and compliance with Chapter 25-8 Subchapter B, (2) easement/access obligations for overhead and underground electric facilities, (3) owner responsibility for erosion control, revegetation, tree protection, and initial tree work within 10 feet of proposed overhead electrical facilities, and (4) owner responsibility for maintaining NESC, OSHA, City of Austin, and Texas state clearances when working near overhead power lines. A 5th note addresses electric facility relocation costs. The notes substantively match the template language with only minor variations in phrasing.
findings.reasoning: The grouping file requires 4 standard Austin Energy notes covering tree pruning/easement rights, easement/access obligations, erosion control responsibilities, and NESC/OSHA clearance maintenance, with approximately 90% semantic matching required. The notes on sheet 5 address all four required topics and preserve the substantive regulatory obligations. Note 1 covers tree pruning rights and references the correct LDC chapter (25-8 Subchapter B). Note 2 covers easement and access requirements for both overhead and underground facilities and references Chapter 25-8. Note 3 addresses erosion control, revegetation, tree protection, and initial tree work responsibilities. Note 4 addresses NESC, OSHA, City rules, and Texas laws regarding clearances near overhead power lines, including the consequence that Austin Energy will not render service if clearances aren't maintained. The semantic match exceeds 90%.
findings.explanation: All 4 required Austin Energy standard notes present on sheet 5 and match template at >90% semantic threshold.

findings.observation: Sheet 8 (Existing Conditions & Demolition Plan) shows existing electric utility facilities. The legend defines symbols for existing overhead electric, existing electric manhole, existing electric meter, existing power pole, and existing guy anchor. The plan depicts: existing power poles along Kinney Avenue on the western boundary; existing overhead utility lines to be removed extending from Kinney Avenue into the property; existing light poles to be removed; underground electric lines to be removed in the central site area; abandoned underground electric lines to be removed near the residence; existing electric meters adjacent to buildings to be removed; and an existing electric manhole near the eastern edge. Electric easements to be released are also labeled.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires that existing electric utility facilities (overhead and underground) be shown on plan sheets. Sheet 8 clearly depicts both overhead and underground existing electric facilities with proper symbols defined in the legend. The plan shows existing power poles, overhead lines, underground lines, manholes, and meters. This provides the information needed for downstream reviewers to verify conflicts, clearances, and service routing. The requirement is satisfied.
findings.explanation: Existing electric facilities (overhead and underground) shown on sheet 8 with legend symbols for poles, lines, manholes, and meters.

findings.observation: Sheet 18 (Overall Utility Plan) shows proposed electric utility facilities. The legend defines symbols for proposed underground electric line (--UGE--), proposed pull box (square with E), proposed electric manhole (circle with E), proposed transformer (square with T), and proposed switchgear (square with S). The plan depicts a major proposed underground electric route running horizontally across the southern portion of the site from the western property line eastward to S. Lamar Blvd. Facilities shown include: three 48-inch electric pull boxes along the southern boundary; three electric manholes along the route near the eastern portion; underground electric line labeled 'SEE PLANS BY OTHERS'; and three variable width electric clearance zones. The routing serves Proposed Building 1.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires that proposed electric utility facilities be shown on plan sheets. Sheet 18 clearly depicts the proposed underground electric infrastructure with proper symbols defined in the legend. The plan shows the routing of underground electric lines, locations of pull boxes and manholes, and required clearance zones. While the detailed electrical design is deferred to 'plans by others' (common practice for MEP consultant-designed systems), the civil site plan properly shows the routing, major infrastructure nodes, and spatial coordination needed for reviewers to verify conflicts and site layout. This satisfies the requirement that proposed electric facilities be depicted on the plan sheets.
findings.explanation: Proposed electric facilities shown on sheet 18 including underground electric route, three pull boxes, three manholes, and clearance zones.

findings.observation: The facts.md file and project README document the site zoning as CS-V-DB90 (Commercial Services, Vertical Mixed Use, Density Bonus 90) for the main tract and CS-V-CO (Commercial Services, Vertical Mixed Use, Conditional Overlay) for the two smaller tracts. The grouping file specifies that AEGB-02 applies only 'If zoned CBD or DMU' (Central Business District or Downtown Mixed Use). The site is not zoned CBD or DMU.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item condition is explicit: the Letter of Intent requirement applies only to sites zoned CBD (Central Business District) or DMU (Downtown Mixed Use). The site has CS-V-DB90 and CS-V-CO zoning, which are commercial/mixed-use zoning districts but not the specific CBD or DMU districts that trigger the LOI requirement at site plan stage. The grouping overview notes that the LOI is required for CBD/DMU sites 'under Downtown Design' and for sites invoking the Downtown Density Bonus Program (DDBP). While this site uses a density bonus program (DB90), the DB90 program is distinct from the Downtown Density Bonus Program referenced in the grouping materials. The condition is not met.
findings.explanation: Site is zoned CS-V-DB90 and CS-V-CO, not CBD or DMU; LOI requirement does not apply.

summary: 4 of 4 applicable items pass. AEGB-02 is not applicable (site not zoned CBD/DMU). All Austin Energy standard notes are present and compliant, and both existing and proposed electric facilities are properly depicted on plan sheets.
